_comment: The programs tier of the corpus gate (RFC 0038, section 5), run by scripts/corpus-gate.py
--programs: large programs WeaveC is not tuned on, pinned by release archive (`url`, `sha256`),
built with their own build systems and CC set to weavec-cc in report mode and, once more, to
the reference compiler, and each run through its own test suite (`test`) with
WEAVEC_RT_REPORT_LOG collecting the reports. `failures` is a regular expression whose first group
names failing tests in the suite's output, separated by white space (several per match).
`referenceFailures` lists, per platform (darwin, linux, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64; the most
specific applies), the tests that fail with the reference compiler on the gate's machines, and
`acceptedFailures`, per platform, the tests that fail with weavec-cc alone for a reason an RFC
accepts (each maps to that reason, which names the RFC), and
`platforms` the build or test commands that replace the program's on a platform. The
gate fails on any report not triaged in triage.json (by the program's name), on any test that
fails with weavec-cc and is not listed, on an accepted test that weavec-cc passes, and on a listed test that the reference build passes or
an unlisted one it fails: the list cannot go stale. `programs` are what the suite needs on
PATH (as in prerequisites.json). Commands run under /bin/sh in the unpacked tree with CC, JOBS,
PREFIX (an installation directory inside the build) and TCL_CONFIG_DIR (the directory of
tclConfig.sh, when one is found) set. `timeout` bounds each command, in seconds. Only the test
suite's reports are judged: those of programs the build runs (configure's probes) are recorded

programs.name: sqlite
programs.notes: SQLite 3.50.4's source release (the corpus has only the amalgamation) and its Tcl test harness; `make quicktest` runs about 330,000 tests through testfixture. On GitHub's macos-15 runners its timed lock tests (busy2, walsetlk) miss their windows under load with any compiler.

darwin.busy2-1.1.3: RFC 0040 section 0: a timed lock wait (busy2 expects 0.95-1.5 s, walsetlk 1-4 s) that the loaded macos-15 runner misses, as it misses its siblings with the reference compiler; walsetlk.test and busy2.test pass alone with weavec-cc in three runs of three
darwin.walsetlk-2.2.14: RFC 0040 section 0: a timed lock wait (busy2 expects 0.95-1.5 s, walsetlk 1-4 s) that the loaded macos-15 runner misses, as it misses its siblings with the reference compiler; walsetlk.test and busy2.test pass alone with weavec-cc in three runs of three

programs.name: cpython
programs.notes: CPython 3.13.7 (on Darwin against Homebrew's OpenSSL 3; 3.13 does not build against OpenSSL 4): an interpreter with its own allocator (pymalloc) over malloc, extension modules built as shared libraries the interpreter loads, and a test suite of about 470 files run in four workers. On Darwin test_compileall fails with the reference compiler too (its quiet-mode test sees a warning from the toolchain).
programs.test: if [ -x python.exe ]; then p=./python.exe; else p=./python; fi; $p -m test -j4 --timeout 900 -u-network,-urlfetch 2>&1 | tail -80

programs.name: postgresql
programs.notes: PostgreSQL 17.6: a server whose memory contexts carve palloc chunks out of malloc'd blocks, run through its main regression suite (pg_regress against a temporary installation). It is installed into the build first, because Darwin's System Integrity Protection drops the library path make check would set.

programs.name: git
programs.notes: git 2.51.0: object parsing, packfiles and a test suite of about 1,000 shell scripts. On Darwin t3900 (i18n commit encodings) and t7528 fail with the reference compiler too. On Linux it builds without curl (NO_CURL), whose headers the gate's machines need not have. git's fsck reads objects from blocks of exactly their size with strcspn, which RFC 0038 section 2 checks over the bytes read.

build: make -j"$JOBS" CC="$CC" NO_GETTEXT=1 NO_TCLTK=1 NO_CURL=1 > build.log

programs.test: cd t && make -k -j"$JOBS" $(ls t[0-9]*.sh) > tests.log 2>&1; make aggregate-results 2>&1 | tail -20

programs.name: coreutils
programs.notes: GNU coreutils 9.5 with gnulib: about 100 programs and 600 test scripts. gnulib's word-at-a-time rawmemchr reads past the string it searches (triaged as the project's bug: ASan stops it too). On Darwin three tests fail with the reference compiler too: sort-debug-keys and sort-h-thousands-sep (the locale's thousands separator) and touch/not-owner. On Linux sort-debug-keys does.

linux.tests/cut/cut-huge-range: RFC 0038, amendment 18: under ulimit -v the shadow cannot be reserved, and the runtime's warning that accesses are not checked is on the stderr the test compares (the test skips under ASan, which refuses to run)
linux.tests/printf/printf-surprise: RFC 0038, amendment 18: under ulimit -v the shadow cannot be reserved, and the runtime's warning that accesses are not checked is on the stderr the test compares (the test skips under ASan, which refuses to run)

programs.name: ninja
programs.notes: ninja 1.13.2 (RFC 0039, section 9), a build system in C++: a manifest lexer and parser, a graph of nodes and edges in hash maps, the build log and deps log (mmap'd, compacted), a subprocess pool, the state of a build. Built with its CMake build and its googletest tests (ninja_test, about 400 tests) against the corpus's googletest checkout ($CORPUS/googletest as FetchContent's source: nothing is downloaded).
programs.test: cd out && ./ninja_test > tests.log 2>&1; s=$?; grep -E '^\[  FAILED  \] ' tests.log | sort -u; tail -3 tests.log; [ $s -eq 0 ] || echo "[  FAILED  ] ninja_test.exit_status_$s"

programs.name: cppcheck
programs.notes: Cppcheck 2.22.0 (RFC 0039, section 9), a static analyzer in C++: a tokenizer over linked lists of tokens, a simplecpp preprocessor, symbol databases of scopes, variables and functions, value flow over std::list and std::unordered_map of values, the checkers, TinyXML-2 and picojson bundled. Built with its makefile; its test is testrunner (about 5,300 tests), whose failures name TestClass::test.
programs.test: ./testrunner > tests.log 2>&1; s=$?; grep -E '^(\S+:[0-9]+\()?Test[A-Za-z0-9_]+::[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\): Assertion| - )' tests.log | sort -u; tail -6 tests.log; [ $s -eq 0 ] || echo "TestRunner::exit_status_$s - Exception"

programs.name: cmake
programs.notes: CMake 4.4.5 (RFC 0039, section 9), a build system generator in C++: a language interpreter over lists of strings, generator expressions, the Makefile and Ninja generators, CTest and CPack, libuv for processes, and bundled C libraries (curl without OpenSSL, libarchive, zlib, zstd, liblzma, expat, jsoncpp, libuv, kwsys). Built by its bootstrap, which builds a first cmake with the compilers and then the rest with it. The test is 140 of its 699 CTest tests that need no network and no other toolchain: the CMakeLib unit tests, kwsys, CMakeOnly, CMakeCommands and the RunCMake suites of the language's commands, the generators, install, presets and ctest (which configure and build small projects with the same compilers, so their programs are guarded too).
programs.test: bin/ctest -j"$JOBS" --timeout 1200 -R '^(CMakeLib|kwsys|CMakeOnly|CMakeCommands)\.|^RunCMake\.(string|list|math|file|file-GET_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCIES|if|while|foreach|function|macro|cmake_language|block|return|message|configure_file|set|unset|cmake_parse_arguments|separate_arguments|get_filename_component|cmake_path|include|option|variable_watch|project|add_library|add_executable|target_sources|target_link_libraries|target_compile_definitions|add_custom_command|add_custom_target|install|CMakePresets|ctest_test|CTestCommandLine|CommandLine|Configure|GeneratorExpression|Make|Ninja)$' > ctest.log 2>&1; grep -E '^\s*[0-9]+ - \S+ \(' ctest.log; tail -12 ctest.log

programs.name: duckdb
programs.notes: DuckDB 1.5.6 (RFC 0039, section 9), an analytical database in C++: vectors of values in buffers from its own buffer manager, an arena allocator per query, a catalog of shared pointers, a parser (the bundled libpg_query), a planner and optimizer, a vectorized and parallel executor, storage with a write-ahead log, and the core_functions and parquet extensions linked in. Built with its CMake Release build (unity sources) and the unittest runner, which runs the fast tests (the sqllogictest files but those named .test_slow, and the C++ tests). The build first fixes a true bug of DuckDB's inequality join (RFC 0039, amendment 17): IEJoinGlobalSourceState reads completed[size_t(stage)] once the stage is DONE, one element past a std::array of DONE elements (physical_iejoin.cpp:279), which the C++ library's check stops on Linux, the whole suite with it, when the join's threads finish in that order; the array gains the element, which starts at zero as the others do. On Darwin the build first undefines the macOS 27 SDK's ERA macro (<xlocale.h>, which libc++ includes, now pulls in <_langinfo.h>) before DuckDB's DatePartSpecifier::ERA, which it otherwise breaks with either compiler.
build: perl -0pi -e 's/(array<atomic<idx_t>, static_cast<size_t>\(IEJoinSourceStage::DONE\))> completed;/$1 + 1> completed;/ or die qq(IEJoin patch did not apply\n)' src/execution/operator/join/physical_iejoin.cpp

perl -0pi -e 's/(array<atomic<idx_t>, static_cast<size_t>\(IEJoinSourceStage::DONE\))> completed;/$1 + 1> completed;/ or die qq(IEJoin patch did not apply\n)' src/execution/operator/join/physical_iejoin.cpp

programs.test: out/test/unittest > tests.log 2>&1; s=$?; grep -E ': FAILED:' tests.log | sort -u; tail -25 tests.log; [ $s -eq 0 ] || echo "FAILED-TEST: unittest.exit_status_$s"
